A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, six figures, two tables, and Appendices A–D are sufficiently readable for reliable comparison, including the new Appendix A.2 in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 privacy-auditing experiments, Gemma 2 finetuning on PersonaChat, and simulations of constructed attacks in Sections 3–4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and simulations, including the results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–6.

M1.justification: The linear-loss privacy heuristic, DP-SGD procedure, and attack constructions are unchanged. Appendix A.2 supplies pseudocode for the computation already described in Appendix A.1; it does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10 image classification, Gemma 2 finetuning on PersonaChat, and the same natural, blank-input, adversarial-gradient, and synthetic counterexample settings.

E2.justification: The standard composition analysis, full-batch DP-GD comparison in Figure 1, and evaluated gradient-space and input-space attacks remain unchanged. The newly cited black-box auditing paper is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The model configurations, batch-size and step sweeps, privacy targets, auditing procedures, and training settings in Appendix D are retained. The added accounting pseudocode does not establish any revision to the reported experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the attack comparisons, batch-size analysis, quadratic-regularizer sensitivity study, and pathological and malicious-dataset counterexamples. Appendix A.2 adds computational documentation, not a new analysis or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both retain PLD auditing with Clopper–Pearson confidence intervals, 512 CIFAR-10 models per canary condition in Section 3.1, and the 100,000-trial constructions. Appendix D's run-count statements are also unchanged; no new uncertainty-reporting practice appears.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–6 retain their results. For example, both report PersonaChat perplexity 24.3 and empirical epsilon 2.1 at batch size 2048, and CIFAR-10 accuracy 79.5% and empirical epsilon 1.7 at batch size 4096. Section 4.2's numerical counterexamples are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, the privacy definitions, Appendix A's proof and derivation, Appendix B's full-batch argument, and Section 4's mathematical counterexamples are retained. The new pseudocode provides implementation detail without revising the formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: a linear-loss heuristic for final-iterate privacy, empirical support from practical attacks, contrived counterexamples, and a target for future auditing and theoretical analysis.

C2.justification: The explanations of attack effectiveness, small quadratic-counterexample violations, and batch-size implications are unchanged. Both versions retain the linearity qualification and acknowledge that the heuristic is not a universal privacy guarantee.

D1.justification: v3 adds Appendix A.2 with explicit likelihood-ratio, inversion, Gaussian-tail, and epsilon/delta accounting routines. v1 supplied formulas and a binary-search description. Hardware, training implementation, computational costs, and accounting-library access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and the bibliography add Annamalai and De Cristofaro's Nearly Tight Black-Box Auditing of Differentially Private Machine Learning. This is a limited citation addition; the broader research positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence remain largely verbatim. Changes include the new Appendix A.2 subsection, minor wording corrections, author-footnote and publication-note edits, and conversion to author–year citations.

P2.justification: v3 substantially restyles the document with different title and author formatting, body and heading typography, spacing, and float arrangement. Figures 2–3 now share a page, and a multipage formatted code listing is added. The existing plot designs and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.2 adds useful implementation guidance, while the scientific evidence and arguments remain unchanged. However, its noise-scaling instruction conflicts with the implemented variance, and line 79 omits the sign required for the reverse-divergence calculation. These new reproducibility problems make it unclear whether the added documentation provides a net quality improvement.
